min_stake_amount.meaning: minimum allowed stake amount of 10 gwei staked by the normal user

tiny_operation_amount.meaning: tiny L1 withdrawal operation amount of 1 in 8 decimals created by queuing the withdrawal

bridge_rejects_tiny.meaning: the L1 bridge rejects the tiny queued operation amount
bridge_rejects_tiny.checkpoint: at L1 bridge processing of the tiny operation

pending_withdrawals_exist.meaning: other users have pending withdrawal requests in the L1 queue
pending_withdrawals_exist.checkpoint: before the tiny operation is processed

recovery_mechanism_available.meaning: a built-in mechanism exists to recover the lost funds without a contract upgrade

assumptions: Production L1 bridges realistically reject the tiny 1-in-8-decimals amount (asm_bridge_rejects_tiny).
The tiny operation is the head of the sequential queue ahead of the pending withdrawals.
The admin queue reset is the only available recovery option and is not shown to have occurred.

unresolved.description: The report states the absence of a built-in recovery mechanism as a qualitative fact without a numeric or structural definition; recovery_mechanism_available is a grounded Boolean for later code binding.

limitations: Formalizes only the i_no_recovery impact (no built-in recovery without contract upgrade); queue blocking and permanent fund loss are separate impacts not covered here.

The condition narrows to the reported incident configuration (10 gwei stake, 1-in-8-decimals operation, bridge rejection, pending withdrawals present) rather than a fully general queue-progress requirement.
recovery_mechanism_available is a report-grounded Boolean; its concrete code-level binding is deferred.
